title: dome-mirror delete-propagation: prune-expired-orphan reconciliation in sync-workspace-step4c.js (DIRECTIVE-20260610-002)
problem: sync-workspace-step4c.js has zero unlink/delete calls — it only propagates copies git→FUSE (build.js syncToWorkspace is copyIfExists + walkAppendOnly, both create-only). When prune-integrity deletes per-run artifacts from origin/main (1,680 files archived 2026-06-10), the FUSE copies persist indefinitely. Measured FUSE orphans at directive time: 955 workspace-sync-runs (794 past retention), 795 verify-pending-run (490 past), 316 narrative-cite-audit (~305 past), est. ~430 MB. PROP-082 correctly prevents the orphans from re-entering git (FUSE→git filter confirmed working via 5/5 GitHub 404 spot-checks), but nothing reclaims the FUSE side.

investigation_answers.q1_mechanism: Chosen: allow-list-restricted full reconciliation (directive option (a), hardened) rather than git-log D-entry parsing (option (b)) or checkout-style sync (option (c)). Rationale: (b) requires a durable baseline SHA; the natural baseline (last sentinel's remote_sha) is fragile under --depth 50 shallow clones (baseline ages out of history → git diff fails → deletions silently never propagate) and misses any backlog accumulated while the pass was broken or disabled. (c) (checkout/rsync --delete semantics) has unbounded blast radius across the whole tree — exactly the 2026-05-21 disaster shape. (a)-restricted is self-healing (each cycle reconciles current state, no bookkeeping), and its blast radius is bounded by THREE independent guards: pattern allow-list (only prune-managed per-run artifact patterns under monitor/integrity/), git-HEAD absence check (git ls-files is the authoritative 'belongs in git' test, not inference from logs), and per-pattern retention age from the filename-embedded date. The age guard is the key insight: monitor/integrity files are BORN on FUSE before workspace-sync pushes them to git, so 'absent from HEAD' alone would delete fresh unpushed sentinels and destroy the audit trail. 'absent from HEAD AND past retention window' is exactly the definition of a prune orphan and excludes every legitimate file state.
investigation_answers.q2_thresholds: abort_abs=500 candidates OR >50% of the category's FUSE file count → abort with zero deletions + sentinel (shape-anomaly guard; workspace-sync's 50/10% is calibrated for git-content deletion which is unrecoverable — here targets are FUSE copies of files already archived to *-archive.jsonl in git, so recoverability is higher and steady-state legitimate volume is larger). Below abort: delete at most per_cycle_cap=200/cycle, truncate remainder to next hourly cycle (self-draining without operator involvement). Steady-state expected volume is ~30-80/day (daily artifact production ≈ daily prune deletions), so 200/cycle ≈ 2.5-6x daily traffic; the current ~1,600-orphan backlog is explicitly out of scope (operator draining concurrently). All three numbers operator-tunable in config.
investigation_answers.q3_path_prefix_opt_in: Yes — opt-in by exact pattern, not just prefix. The DELETE_PATTERNS table lists 6 patterns mirroring workspace-sync.md is_prune_expired() and prune-integrity.js POLICIES (edit-one-edit-all-three note added to all sites). Deliberately excluded: report-*.json (90d), workspace-sync-abort-*.json (30d), sync-workspace-non-ff-abort-*.json (90d) — low-volume, high-forensic-value; manual cleanup is fine. Maintenance cost of updating the table when prune gains a category is accepted: a missed new category degrades to the status quo (accumulation), never to over-deletion. Fail-safe direction is correct.
investigation_answers.q4_prop082_interaction: No PROP-082 change required for the core loop: once dome-mirror unlinks a FUSE orphan there is nothing for universal-pusher to push, and before deletion PROP-082's is_prune_expired already blocks re-push of every file our rule would delete (our age criterion is the same windows). One pre-existing wrinkle flagged, not fixed here: narrative-cite-audit is pruned by COUNT (keep_last_n=7, retention_days=null) but is_prune_expired/our rule use a 14-DAY window — a file pruned by count while younger than 14d is invisible to both filters: PROP-082 could re-push it to git (pre-existing gap) and our pass would not delete it until day 15 (bounded lingering, then converges). Recommend a follow-up one-liner aligning is_prune_expired's narrative-cite-audit window to 7d if the re-push case is ever observed; not bundled here to keep this PROP single-purpose.
investigation_answers.fuse_unlink_caveat: CLAUDE.md documents the FUSE mount as not supporting unlink() for git operations, and the operator drains the current backlog via mcp__cowork__allow_cowork_file_delete — so fs.unlinkSync from the helper MAY fail with EPERM in dome-mirror's session. The pass probes this empirically: on the first EPERM-class error it stops, records 'unlink-unsupported-on-fuse' in the sentinel, and degrades to manifest-only mode. Even permanent manifest-only mode is a win: it converts invisible accumulation into a visible, machine-readable deletion queue the operator (or a future allow_cowork_file_delete-granted step in dome-mirror.md) can act on. Whether to grant dome-mirror automated delete permission is an operator decision — see why_human_needed.

proposed_fix.summary: Add a deletePropagationPass(fuseRoot) function to sync-workspace-step4c.js, invoked only in the needSync branch immediately after a successful 'node build.js sync-workspace', with results merged into the existing single sentinel (new 'delete_propagation' key — preserves the exactly-one-sentinel invariant). Pass is config-gated: ships with enabled=false (manifest-only). Three-guard candidate rule: allow-listed pattern AND absent from git ls-files HEAD AND past per-pattern retention per filename date. Safety gates per PROP-051 lineage: abort sentinel above 500 candidates or 50% of category, truncate-at-200 per cycle below that, EPERM fallback to manifest-only. No changes to dome-mirror.md procedure (same single helper invocation), no changes to prune-integrity.js, dome-mirror stays a FULL clone.

safety_gates.inherited_constraints: Disaster-sensitivity per DIRECTIVE-20260610-002 constraints: delete-sanity abort threshold, working-tree-size check (dome-mirror Step 1 already enforces >=100 tracked files before the helper runs — a partial clone makes git ls-files small, which would mark MORE files as orphans, so the existing gate is load-bearing for this pass and is called out as such), abort sentinel on suspicious volume (merged into the run sentinel with aborted reason + zero deletions). dome-mirror remains a FULL clone per PROP-051 lineage — sparse-checkout would empty git ls-files for monitor/integrity and the pass would classify everything as orphaned; the abort_pct gate (50%) would catch this, but the FULL-clone rule is the primary defense and is restated in the code comment.
safety_gates.force_push_edge: A force-pushed/reset origin is classified true-non-ff by the existing Step 4 logic and the helper exits 1 BEFORE the needSync branch — the delete pass never runs against rewritten history. Additionally, because the candidate rule checks current HEAD membership (not historical D entries), a file 'reverted away but still belongs' is simply a file absent from HEAD: if it is also past retention it matches prune policy and deleting it is correct by definition; if it is within retention it is kept. There is no state in which the pass deletes a file that current origin/main says should exist.

test_plan: T1 single-file positive: in a scratch clone+fake-FUSE dir, create monitor/integrity/sync-workspace-runs-2026-05-01T00-00-00Z.json on the fake FUSE only (not in git). Run pass with enabled=false → sentinel lists exactly 1 candidate. Flip enabled=true → file unlinked, deleted=1.

T2 fresh-FUSE-born negative: create monitor/integrity/sync-workspace-runs-<today>Z.json on fake FUSE only. Run pass → 0 candidates (age guard). This is the audit-trail-protection case and MUST pass before any rollout.
T3 in-HEAD negative: pick a real tracked monitor/integrity file present in both → 0 candidates (HEAD-membership guard).
T4 cap/abort: synthesize 600 dated-old fake-FUSE orphans → aborted='delete-sanity gate...', deleted=0. Then 300 orphans → first cycle deletes 200 with truncated=true, second cycle deletes 100.
T5 force-push edge: point a scratch clone at a branch, force-reset upstream, run helper → exits 1 with non-ff-abort sentinel; grep confirms delete pass never logged (it lives after the abort).

T6 EPERM probe (real FUSE, Phase 1): run with enabled=true against the real workspace WITHOUT allow_cowork_file_delete → expect either real deletions (FUSE permits unlink for cowork-session writes) or aborted='unlink-unsupported-on-fuse' + intact files; both outcomes are safe and the sentinel records which world we are in.
T7 undated-filename negative: create monitor/integrity/push-failure-nodate.json on fake FUSE → 0 candidates (undated → never touch).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (land, inert): merge script+config with enabled=false. Every dome-mirror cycle now writes delete_propagation.{candidates,sample} into its sentinel. Zero behavior change to FUSE.

Phase 1 (observe, >=3 days): operator reviews manifests across >=3 days of sentinels. Acceptance: zero false positives (no fresh FUSE-born file ever listed; cross-check any listed file against the corresponding *-archive.jsonl in git). Run T6 probe once manually to learn the FUSE unlink answer.

Phase 2 (enable): operator flips enabled=true via clone-and-push (config is git-owned). If T6 showed unlink-unsupported, instead add an allow_cowork_file_delete grant step to dome-mirror.md Step 1 — this is the operator judgment call below — or accept permanent manifest-only mode and drain via a weekly operator action from the manifest.

Phase 3 (verify): tinker Mode 3 checks 7 days post-enable that FUSE monitor/integrity file count tracks git's (steady state, no growth trend) and that no abort sentinels fired. Add a one-line check to the Mode 2 quick-check block if drift recurs.
Pause/rollback: flip enabled=false (single config push); the pass is stateless so disable is instant and complete.
tradeoffs: Gain: FUSE stops accumulating ~430 MB/month-scale orphan mass; disk-pressure incidents (DIRECTIVE-20260508-001 lineage) lose a contributing source; FUSE listings of monitor/integrity become trustworthy again for agents that read it. Lose/risk: a 3-site pattern-table mirror that can drift (mitigated: drift degrades to accumulation, never over-deletion); reconciliation walks ~2-3K FUSE files per cycle (one readdir walk + one git ls-files — negligible vs the existing build.js sync); if FUSE unlink turns out unsupported the deletion half is inert and we have only bought a manifest (still net-positive but does not close the directive's gap without the follow-up permission decision).
estimated_impact: ~430 MB FUSE reclamation potential at current backlog scale; prevents indefinite future growth (~1-2 MB/day steady state, more when narrative-cite-audit bodies land); removes a recurring tinker/integrity false-signal source (FUSE-vs-git divergence findings).
why_human_needed: Two decisions: (1) approve the rollout gates and thresholds (abort_abs=500 / pct=50 / cap=200) — these are calibrated from current category sizes (~2-3K files) per the directive's Q2 prompt but the operator may prefer tighter; (2) decide the Phase-2 unlink-permission question — granting an automated Haiku agent delete capability inside the workspace is exactly the class of power the 2026-05-21 postmortem says to gate deliberately. Manifest-only forever is a legitimate conservative answer.
